Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaCorp Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaCorp's Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NovaCorp delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover five key aspects:
1. Performance by key categories and brands.
2. Decomposition of organic sales growth into volume, price, and mix.
3. Pricing actions taken and their impact on sales.
4. Competitive activity and our responses.
5. Capital expenditure plans and priorities for the year ahead.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 4.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin expanded to 38.2%, driven by favorable pricing realization, supply chain productivity gains, and a shift toward premium products. Operating income reached $450 million, up 8% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me start with performance across our key categories and brands, which highlights the strength and balance in our portfolio amid a challenging CPG landscape. We're tracking organic net sales growth—volume, mix, and pricing—alongside market share from Nielsen and IRI, distribution gains, and household penetration. In Q3, our core categories achieved aggregate organic growth of 5.2%, surpassing the broader CPG market's 2.8% amid inflation and changing consumer habits. This came from volume gains in premium areas and average pricing actions of 4.1%.

Breaking it down, Beauty & Personal Care, 42% of net sales, grew organically 7.1%. Volume rose 3.2%, mix shifted 2.4% to prestige lines, and pricing added 1.5%. Nielsen shows market share up 110 basis points to 14.2% in measured channels, thanks to innovation. FreshGlow Skincare surged 12.4% with our microbiome-balancing serum using BioShield technology from fermented rice postbiotics, tapping the $15 billion clean beauty market at 9% CAGR and lifting North American household penetration 15%. VitaLocks Hair Care advanced 8.7%, aided by an AI personalization app linking with Ulta and Sephora for shade-matching, raising repeat buys 22%.

North America led at +9.2% with salon recovery, EMEA at +6.8% via EcoRefill pouches cutting plastic 35% for EU compliance and Gen Z appeal. Asia-Pacific stabilized despite China's soft skincare (-1.2%) through Tmall KOL partnerships.

Household & Fabric Care, 35% of sales, posted 4.3% organic growth despite input inflation, via efficiencies and EDLP. Volume edged up 0.1%, mix +2.8% to pods and concentrates, pricing +1.4%. IRI notes 80 basis points share gain to 16.5%, especially laundry velocity up 4%. SparkleClean Laundry rose 6.2% with UltraConcentrate pods outperforming Tide in lab tests on enzymes, hitting 92% ACV in Walmart and Kroger with 10% more shelf space after $120 million R&D. PureShield Disinfectants jumped 9.1% with EPA-registered 24-hour antiviral formula grabbing share from Clorox in a 5% growing market.

LATAM excelled at +7.5% via Brazil sachets boosting rural reach 18%, North America +4.1%, EMEA +2.9% addressing phosphate regs with $50 million reformulations by FY25.

Nutrition & Snacks, 23% of sales, grew 3.8% despite at-home normalization and private labels. Volume -0.5% lapping peaks, mix +2.7% to protein lines, pricing +1.6%. IRI share up 40 basis points to 11.8%. NutriCrunch Protein Bars led +11.2% in $30 billion functional snacks with plant-based 20g protein no-sugar bars certified Clean Label, beating Kind and RXBAR by 2.3 points in convenience. ZestQuench Beverages +5.4% with adaptogen-infused low-cal sparkling waters via PepsiCo vending ties. Divested ClassicChips to focus high-velocity SKUs. APAC +6.1% with NutriCrunch K-pop boosts on Coupang 25% e-comm growth; North America +2.2% prompting Healthify reformulations under 150 calories for 15% Q4 volume rebound.

E-commerce is now 18% of sales, up from 12%, via Shopify and ML forecasting at 8.2x inventory turns. 65% recyclable packaging supports 2030 net-zero, resonating with 72% consumers. Emerging markets get 25% of $2 billion innovation budget; more $500 million divestitures fund M&A like Korean beauty tech. Q4 organic 4-6%, EPS +8-10% assuming stable inputs.

Now, unpacking our organic sales growth of 5.2% for the quarter, ahead of guidance and accelerating for the third straight period. This reflects portfolio resilience against inflation and sentiment softness. Volume grew 2.1% globally, up from Q2's 0.8%, via distribution and innovation offsetting staples weakness. Snacks & Confectionery (35% sales) volume +3.5% on HealthBurst nut bars at 85% North America ACV, gaining 120 basis points MMS vs. Mars, Mondelez per IRI, with 15% e-comm lift on Amazon, Instacart.

Beverages (28%) +1.8% on AquaVital electrolyte sparklers triple-digit in APAC. Household & Personal Care flat on Europe destocking, but +0.5% from EcoShield pods with 40% higher repeats per Nielsen. North America 2.5% on grocery/club; EMEA flat on laundry energy costs; LATAM 4.2% festive prep; APAC 3.1% India rural to 2.5 million outlets.

Price/mix drove 3.1%, pricing 2.4% from 4-6% list hikes like 5% on NovaChips, elasticity -0.3 via NovaRewards app (25 million users). Mix +0.7% premium +12% vs. flat core, VitaGlow skincare +18% ASP, post-divestitures echoing P&G superiority. Snacks 3.8%, Beverages 2.9% RTD coffee, Household 2.5% hypoallergenic pods.

Tailwinds: Innovation 22% sales <36 months old, 300 bps MMS; e-comm 18% (up 400 bps), 2.5x DTC velocity like Unilever; S&OP OTIF 96% from 88%, COGS inflation 1.2% vs. 7%. Q4 mid-single digits, hedged 80% FX, 14 quarters share stability.

On pricing actions, these were central to our 4.2% net sales to $2.85 billion, organic 3.8%. ASP +6.1%, offset by -1.9% volume (better than -3.5% category per Circana), +0.6% mix. Over 18 months, three waves 12-15% hikes, Q2 latest on non-promoted like 5-8% Peak Refresh water, CrunchMax bars; premium 3-4%. AI dynamic pricing with NielsenIQ/SAP Ariba uses IRI, commodity curves.

NGP +5.8% seq., $175 million revenue from pricing (60% organic). Snacks/beverages (65%) pricing +7.2%, volume -0.4%; Household elasticity -4.1% on 6.8% price, +2.1% sales via EcoPure pods.

North America (45%) +6.5% ASP, 4.1% sales $1.28B, EDLP 70% SKUs, trade spend 22% NGPs, 98% salty share vs. Mondelez, elasticity -0.6x vs. Unilever -1.2x, promo resets +2% mix. EMEA flat €650M, 8.2% pricing >Nestlé, -3.7% volume 1.4x elasticity vs. Aldi/Lidl; value engineering €2.49 shampoos, 10% cocoa savings. LATAM 7.3% $420M, 9.1% pricing Brazil/Mexico, -1.2% volume premium 18% mix. APAC 8.6% $500M, 10%+ Tmall snacks no volume loss, millennials +22% incidence.

Ahead, 4-6% H1'25 hikes protecting margins as steel -8%, PET -12%; ML elasticity ZIP-level, 200 bps NGP, 50 bps share like P&G. Margins to 38.2% +110 bps.

Turning to competitive activity, the sector saw intense pressure from inflation, value-seeking, private labels. IRI U.S. category +1.8%, privates +120 bps to 18.5%, 22% staples; Kantar Europe discounters Aldi/Lidl ACV pressure.

P&G EDLP 10-15% Tide reductions +90 bps to 32% share; Mondelez +8% trade Oreo/Ritz +2 velocity, -150 bps margins. We held 85% list prices, premium Vitality Organics +15% units at 12% premium. Trade $450M +5%, ROI +12% AI/NielsenIQ, +1.5 pts salty share, <2% leakage.

Nestlé Vital-Protein cereals +3% Europe; PepsiCo zero Gatorade -1.2 pts our hydration. Our 18 SKUs: CleanBurst plant enzymes vs. Ariel +25% dist. 4 weeks, +8% household; DTC kombucha +35% QoQ e-comm, +0.8 pts functional.

North America privates -0.5 pts, shelf resets +2200 facings ACV 92%, FreshGlow +7%. Europe Unilever Dove refills +4%, our POD/Tesco 1500 stores flat share +€25M. China Liby dupes, SilkSoft humid formula +12% Tmall Gen Z 18%. LATAM Colgate sachets, nano-packs +3 pts velocity.

Fortress Portfolio: 15% R&D ($120M) digital analytics SAP/Blue Yonder predict pricing 72hr 95% hit. 25% recycled packaging FY25 wins Target/Carrefour. Ahead easing pressures CPI 2.5% H2, $200M media +10% 2-3 pts share FY25, $1.2B cash M&A plant proteins. +220 bps EPS.

Finally, our FY2025 capex outlook $1.25B, +12% from $1.12B FY2024, ROIC >12%, stress-tested ocean +5-7%, palm/PET inflation, vs. P&G/Unilever. Capex/sales 4.5% <5.2% peer, utilization 92%.

Priority 1 Manufacturing 45% $560M: $250M Reno greenfield plant-based nutrition/snacks 20% volume, almond/protein 15% IRI outperf. Rotterdam $150M fabric cleaners pods +25% capacity. Vietnam $100M hygiene +8% SE Asia share. Brazil $60M low-sugar RTD 12% CAGR. Payback 3-4yr, EBITDA 22-25%.

Priority 2 Supply Chain 25% $310M: US Midwest $120M micro-ful DCs robotics DTC 18% NA sales +6pts. Poland $90M cold-chain nutrition -30% transit. India/Indo $70M auto DCs 500 SKUs 8.5x turns. Mexico $30M port warehouse. AI demand like PepsiCo -40% stockouts -10% WC.

Priority 3 Digital 20% $250M: $100M robotics/IoT 15 plants cobots -15% labor +18% OEE Ohio pilot. $80M SAP S/4HANA ML maint $50M savings like Colgate. China $50M digital twins energy -10% elec.

Priority 4 Sustainability 10% $130M: $60M solar/heat pumps 5 US plants -25% Scope1/2 IRA credits. $40M recyclable mono-pouches Olay EU PPWR. Singapore $30M anti-aging 10 formulations.

70% organic growth, 30% cost-out +200bps EBITDA 18.5% FY26. Flex ±10% Q4 vis, ROIC hurdles. 6-8% >GDP FY27 premium 35% health. Geopol APAC +5% buffer 60/40 nearshoring.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Mike. We saw strong performance in our FreshGlow and SparkleClean brands this quarter. Our recent GlowUp campaign has resonated well with consumers, driving awareness up 25% and trial 18% per Nielsen. We are also excited about the launch of our new BioShield Serum, which is already generating positive feedback with early sell-through exceeding expectations by 30%. This innovation is contributing to category outperformance and strengthening our premium positioning.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Lisa Chen:
Good morning, John. The GlowUp campaign leverages digital storytelling around clean beauty routines, integrated across social, retail media, and in-store activations. We've partnered with influencers reaching 50 million Gen Z impressions, tying into our BioShield tech. Impact-wise, it's lifted FreshGlow sales 12% in launch markets, with e-comm conversion up 22% via personalized AR try-ons. Early ROI is strong at 3.5x, supporting sustained investment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan.

Emily Davis:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Mike Thompson:
Thanks, Emily. We're proactively hedging key inputs like palm oil and PET at 80% coverage, drawing from lessons in our capex supply chain builds. Dynamic pricing tools allow micro-adjustments, and we've locked savings via supplier renegotiations—10% on cocoa analogs. Combined with productivity from digital upgrades, we expect to limit COGS inflation to 1-2% even if commodities rise another 5%, protecting our 38%+ margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays.

Robert Lee:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, Robert. Inflation is testing trade-down behaviors, but our premium lines like NutriCrunch and VitaGlow are holding resilient with +12% growth, thanks to superior innovation and loyalty via NovaRewards. Elasticity remains favorable at -0.4x in snacks/beauty, outpacing peers, as consumers prioritize health and efficacy. We're gaining share in these segments, with 35% portfolio premiumization as a buffer.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Anna Patel:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Lisa Chen:
Hi, Anna. E-commerce hit 18% of sales, up from 12% YoY, driven by DTC integrations and platforms like Tmall, Amazon. Velocity is 2.5x brick-and-mortar, with personalization and same-day fulfillment from micro-DCs boosting it. Key wins: 35% QoQ in kombucha extensions, 25% NutriCrunch on Coupang. We're targeting 22% by FY25 with more AI recs and omnichannel.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaCorp Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
